Heat flows from a region of higher temperature to one of lower temperature, so heat will flow from gas Y (at 2T) to gas X (at T). The internal energy of an ideal gas is proportional to the product of the number of particles and the absolute temperature (U ∝ NT). Comparing the two gases, = U ∝ * T and = U/2 ∝ * 2T. Solving for the number of particles shows = 4 * , meaning gas X has more particles.

question.html:
An ideal gas X at temperature T has internal energy U. A second ideal gas Y at temperature 2T has internal energy U/2. Which gas has more particles and what is the direction of heat flow between the gases once they are put into thermal contact?

OptionGas with more particlesDirection of heat flow
AXX to Y
BYX to Y
CXY to X
DYY to X
